name: Solange Vunipola-Tremblay
role: Neighborhood council chair and policy advocate for the Highland Park Autonomous Zone
location: Highland Park Autonomous Zone, Council Hall (a reclaimed gymnasium above a hydroponic market)
description:
Solange is a tall, stately woman with warm brown skin, deep-set eyes framed by pronounced crow's feet she treats as credentials, and silver-white locs piled into an architectural structure secured with copper wire and small enamel political pins from campaigns spanning forty years. She moves through Highland Park with the unhurried authority of someone who owns nothing but is trusted with everything. Her geneware is subtle: a faint cat-ear modification — velvet-tipped, tawny — that she got as a young woman and has never seen reason to remove; they swivel slightly when she's listening hard, which unsettles people who don't know to expect it.

Solange has outlasted six Axiom zone managers, three rounds of 'redevelopment consultations,' two assassination attempts she refuses to characterize as such on the record, and one recall election she won by thirty-one votes. She does not call herself a radical. She calls herself a constitutionalist — meaning she holds the HPAZ's founding community charter as sacred and will use every procedural mechanism available to defend it. This makes her less exciting than firebrands and more dangerous than anyone gives her credit for.

core_fears: Highland Park being absorbed into a corponation zone in her lifetime — losing the thing she spent her life building
becoming the institution she fought against, too comfortable and too accommodating
core_desires: genuine self-determination for HPAZ — not autonomy on a corponation's sufferance, but real legal sovereignty
to step down voluntarily, on her own terms, when she has someone worthy to hand the charter to
coping_mechanisms: procedural focus — when overwhelmed, she returns to the rules, the charter, the process
gardening in the council hall's small rooftop plot; refuses to rush it
blind_spots: believes deeply in process in ways that can make her slow to act when speed is what's needed
has a blind spot for younger organizers who remind her of herself — prone to over-investing
psychology.secret: In 2193, during a critical funding crisis, she accepted a conditional grant from a Palladian subsidiary to keep the HPAZ health clinic open. The conditions included a non-disclosure clause and a right-of-first-refusal on a small parcel of zone land. She has never told the council. The clause is still active and Palladian has not yet invoked it — but she knows they haven't forgotten.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Formal and measured; parliamentary language mixed with warm community idiom; occasional Fijian phrases inherited from her paternal grandmother; never curses in public
speech_patterns.cadence: Unhurried, rhythmic — she was a public speaker before she was a politician and it shows; knows how to fill silence without rushing it
verbal_tics: a slight pause and cat-ear swivel when she's genuinely surprised by something
example_lines: 'I've been called a moderate so many times I've started to think it means something different than they intend. I have not moderated my goals. I have moderated my impatience.'
'You want to burn it down. I understand that. But someone has to be standing here when the smoke clears, ready to build something that holds.'

story_hooks: Palladian has quietly activated the clause in their 2193 agreement and is preparing to claim the parcel — which now sits directly beneath a beloved clinic. Solange needs help untangling this without her past compromise becoming public.

A faction within the council is pushing to recall her, backed by outside money she suspects comes from a corponation using local proxies; she needs someone to trace it without triggering a public crisis.
narrative_function: Local authority figure and quest giver; her procedural knowledge makes her invaluable for navigating zone politics; she can open or close doors depending on whether players have earned her trust; represents the slow, grinding work of institutional resistance.
augmentations: Cosmetic cat-ear geneware (tawny, velvet-tipped, functional swivel); basic cardiac monitor implant (medical necessity, post-stress episode 2196); reading-assist optical overlay for document review — standard elder-care tier
daily_life: Holds open constituent hours from early morning in the council hall; spends afternoons in procedural meetings, document review, and negotiation calls with corponation liaisons and city administrators; evenings are reserved for community events, which she attends as a participant, not a speaker.
affiliation: Highland Park Autonomous Zone Community Council (Chair); Meridian 88 Non-Corporate Zone Solidarity Network; informal mentor to several younger organizers citywide

decision_rules: Follow the charter — it exists to constrain everyone including herself
Never make a decision under duress without at minimum asking for twenty-four hours
Protect the community's capacity to self-govern above any single outcome
escalation_ladder: Listens and asks procedural clarifying questions
Calls a formal meeting to address the issue collectively
Engages allied zone councils and media contacts
Invokes the charter's emergency provisions and takes direct community action

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Courteous and formal, slightly distant — reserves warmth as something that must be earned rather than assumed
interpersonal_modes.friends: Disarmingly funny and direct; drops the formal register entirely; shows care through frank, sometimes brutal honesty

stress_responses.medium: Goes very still, speaks more slowly, asks more questions than she answers
stress_responses.high: Removes herself physically from the situation for exactly fifteen minutes, then returns with a decision

contradictions: Champions radical community self-determination but is deeply uncomfortable with tactics that fall outside formal process
Presents as supremely confident in public while being privately consumed by doubt about specific past decisions
habits: Reviews the HPAZ founding charter every Sunday morning — physically, the original printed document
Keeps a small clay E.L.F. figurine on her council desk as a ward against network intrusion; pours a few drops of water on it before difficult meetings
Addresses everyone, even opponents, by their preferred name and title — it disarms and obligates simultaneously
breaking_points: Learning that someone used the council's trust to harm a constituent
Being publicly called a corponation collaborator — the secret she carries makes the accusation unbearable even when leveled falsely

cyberware_inventory.condition: functional, sends alerts to her personal device

timeline.event: Born in what was then the Highland Park refugee resettlement zone
Participates in the first HPAZ charter drafting committee at age 19
Elected to the neighborhood council for the first time
Accepts Palladian conditional grant during funding crisis; non-disclosure signed
Stress-related cardiac episode; takes six weeks off — the only time she has done so
Survives recall election by 31 votes; interprets it as a mandate and a warning simultaneously
